_description: Part 9 companion to search-facets.json - that file lists WHAT the facet values and counts are; this file defines HOW selecting more than one value, or values across different facets, combines. Computed directly against search-index.json (520 real documents), not assumed - see verification notes on each rule.

cardinalityPerDocument._description: Whether a single document can carry more than one value for a given facet dimension - this determines what 'select two values in the same facet' even means. Verified by computing the max array length for each field across all 520 documents.

singleValued.verified: max array length = 1 for every one of these fields across all 520 documents - a document has exactly one (or zero, if genuinely unclassifiable) value per dimension.

multiValued.verified: metric: up to 5 values on one document (ab-test:AB-001 has 5 real KPI labels - primaryKpi + 4 otherKpis). tags: up to 11 values on one document (calculator:ctr has 11 real cross-referenced calculator-family tags). This matters for AND/OR semantics below - a multi-valued field participates in a cross-dimension AND as 'does this document have ANY of its own several values matching the selected set', not 'does it have exactly one'.

withinOneFacet_semantics: OR. Selecting multiple values within the SAME facet dimension (e.g. type=calculator + type=ab-test, or surface=cart + surface=checkout) returns documents matching ANY of the selected values in that dimension - the standard, expected faceted-search convention, and the only sensible one for single-valued dimensions (a document literally cannot be type=calculator AND type=ab-test at once, so AND-within-a-single-valued-dimension would always return zero and is never the intended behavior). For the two multi-valued dimensions (metric, tags), OR-within-facet is still the recommendation for the same reason a design would expect: 'documents about metric=CAC or metric=ROAS' is the useful question, not 'documents whose KPI list literally contains every one of the selected metrics simultaneously' (that second interpretation is technically also implementable if a future design genuinely needs it, but it's a stricter, less common expectation and should be an explicit, separately-flagged filter mode if ever added - not the default).
acrossFacets_semantics: AND. Selecting values in two or more DIFFERENT facet dimensions (e.g. type=calculator AND normalizedCategory=cart-and-checkout) narrows the result set to documents matching the within-facet OR result of EVERY selected dimension - i.e. (type OR-set) AND (normalizedCategory OR-set) AND (surface OR-set)... This is the standard interpretation and matches how search-facets.json's own documentCount numbers were computed (single-dimension, no cross-filtering) - cross-dimension AND is a logical, not yet separately validated, extension of that same per-dimension counting.

multiSelectByDimension.note: All 9 dimensions support multi-select under the OR-within-facet rule above. Whether a given design actually EXPOSES multi-select UI (vs. single-select radio-style) for a given facet is a design decision (see SEARCH-DESIGN-HANDOFF.md's DESIGN FREEDOM section) - this only says the underlying data/logic supports it uniformly, so the UI is free to choose per facet without needing a data change later.

zeroResultCombinations._description: Computed directly by cross-tabulating type against each of the 4 shared facet dimensions (normalizedCategory, surface, funnelStage, businessObjective) across all 520 real documents - not estimated. A large fraction of type-x-dimension pairs are genuinely zero, because several dimensions are corpus-specific by construction (surface is populated almost entirely from ab-test's own surface field; funnelStage and businessObjective lean heavily journey/ab-test; normalizedCategory has real gaps per corpus - see search-facets.json's own per-value counts).

computedCounts.note: e.g. ab-test x advertising-and-media = 0, blog-article x acquisition-and-onboarding = 0. Non-zero e.g. ab-test x search-and-discovery = 72, ab-test x acquisition-and-onboarding = 53.

surface is populated almost exclusively by ab-test documents (see SEARCH-DESIGN-HANDOFF.md's own note: 'surface (14 values, ab-test only)') - e.g. blog-article x cart = 0, blog-article x checkout = 0, for every one of the 14 surface values against every non-ab-test type.

e.g. ab-test x activation-onboarding = 0, ab-test x cross-lifecycle = 0 (ab-test only reaches 3 of the 5 stage values: acquisition-qualification=53, ending-closure=4, engagement-retention=22). journey x cross-lifecycle = 216 is the single largest non-zero pair in the whole facet system.

the most sparse cross-tab of the four - e.g. ab-test x cancellation-termination = 0, ab-test x change-versioning = 0 (ab-test concentrates almost entirely in review-required=166 and risk-compliance=45).

zeroResultCombinations.policy: A facet UI MUST NOT present a value combination as freely selectable without regard to context, because most type-x-dimension pairs are genuinely zero (see counts above) - a static 'show every value in every facet at all times, unfiltered' design would routinely walk a user into a dead end. The data-layer recommendation (not a UI mandate - see DESIGN FREEDOM) is CONTEXTUAL/DYNAMIC facet value counts: after every filter selection, recompute each remaining facet's available values and counts against the CURRENTLY FILTERED result set, not the full 520-document corpus. A value whose contextual count would be 0 should either be hidden or shown visibly disabled with its real 0 - never silently offered as if it might return something. This requires no new data (search-index.json already carries every field needed to recompute any cross-tab live) - it's a computation the query-time layer runs, not a static payload search-facets.json needs to pre-enumerate for every combination (the combinatorial space - 9 dimensions, some with hundreds of values - makes pre-computing every N-way intersection impractical and unnecessary).
zeroResultCombinations.fallbackForAZeroResultSelection: If a user combination genuinely lands on 0 results anyway (e.g. via a multi-select path that wasn't gated by contextual counts, or a future facet added without this contract being re-applied), the correct behavior is the same 'filtered no results' state defined in the empty/no-result behavior contract (Part 12, forthcoming in this round's remaining tasks) - not a silent fallback to unfiltered results and not a fabricated suggestion. Deterministic only: e.g. 'remove one of your N filters' framed generically, never a specific alternative invented at runtime.

notDecided: This file does not decide facet UI presentation (chips, dropdowns, an accordion, a sidebar, a bottom sheet), the order facets are shown in, default-expanded/collapsed state, or which of the 9 dimensions a first design iteration chooses to expose at all (a design is free to launch with only type + normalizedCategory and add more later - see SEARCH-DESIGN-HANDOFF.md's DESIGN FREEDOM section) - those remain open, as required.
